# Template quality bar

Date: 2026-10-30. Status: proposal. Every template must pass every line before it ships in Studio's start screen. A
reviewer (human or a separate AI session, never the author alone) ticks each line and links the evidence: a test run,
a screenshot or a timing. "Not checked" is a fail.

Conventions these checks refer to: `docs/templates/README.md`.

## A. First minute

- [ ] From the start screen, "Make it mine" to a running game takes at most 2 clicks and no typing. Default project
      name and folder are filled in.
- [ ] On the reference PC the project opens in under 5 s and Play starts in under 3 s.
- [ ] Within 10 s of pressing Play, a new player knows the goal. The HUD or a one-line prompt says it in under 10 words.
- [ ] Within 30 s of Play, the player has done the core action once (jumped a gap, fired, found an item, placed a block).
- [ ] No empty screen at any point: no black viewport while loading, no blank panel, no "nothing here" without a next
      step.

## B. Playable and finished

- [ ] The game loop completes: you can win or finish, and the game resets or offers "play again" without restarting
      Studio.
- [ ] Solo works. If the genre needs more players (team shooter, party rounds), the template fills the gap
      (solo practice mode, warm-up round) instead of a lobby that waits forever.
- [ ] Multiplayer works with the stated `players_max` in a local server-and-clients test (from milestone 2): no
      duplicated rewards, no desync of score or round state, late joiners get the current state.
- [ ] Every RemoteEvent handler on the server checks type, range, rate and ownership as listed in the template doc.
      A test fires each remote with bad data and expects a refusal and no state change.
- [ ] Death, respawn and leaving mid-round never leave the game stuck (no round that never ends, no plot that stays
      claimed by a player who left).
- [ ] Runs at 60 fps or more at 1080p high on the reference PC (RTX 3060 Ti class) with `players_max` characters,
      and the fps target for integrated graphics is measured or marked "not verified".
- [ ] No placeholder text, debug prints, "TODO", lorem ipsum or test parts visible to players.

## C. Easy to make it yours

- [ ] Game settings panel shows 6 to 15 knobs with labels and help text. Each knob, at its minimum and its maximum,
      leaves a playable game (smoke test runs both extremes of the three main knobs).
- [ ] Every look preset applies cleanly: no part left in a colour that clashes, hazards stay readable as hazards,
      goals stay readable as goals, UI text keeps 4.5:1 contrast. Screenshot per preset.
- [ ] Renaming the game, changing the thumbnail and applying a look each take one action.
- [ ] Parts that a creator would want to recolour, resize or duplicate are plain Parts in clearly named Folders, not
      buried in Models or generated by scripts at runtime. Things that must be generated (procedural maps, enemies)
      have a visible "spawn point" or "template" Instance the creator can edit.
- [ ] Swap-in assets: every visual made from Parts sits in one Model with a clear name (`ViewModels.Rifle`,
      `Enemies.Crawler`) so a creator can replace it with their own Model of the same name without touching code.

## D. Code a beginner can read

- [ ] Every script's first line says what it does in one sentence.
- [ ] Every script has 2 or 3 `-- TRY:` lines that work: changing the value as suggested makes a visible difference on
      the next Play.
- [ ] No script longer than about 200 lines; shared logic is in ModuleScripts with one job each.
- [ ] Server decides, client shows: no money, health, score, inventory or round state changes in a LocalScript.
- [ ] Names follow the convention (`...Service`, `...Controller`, `Remotes.<WhatHappened>`).
- [ ] Only API members that exist in `docs/luau-api.md` for the target milestone. No hidden engine hooks a creator
      could not write themselves.
- [ ] No code copied from another engine's samples or another game. Reviewer spot-checks three scripts.

## E. Teaches while you play

- [ ] `tutorial.toml` has 5 to 7 steps following the arc: play, restyle, tune, build, change one line, play again,
      share.
- [ ] Each step's text is 25 words or fewer and its completion check fires (tested by a scripted Studio run).
- [ ] Skipping or closing the tutorial never breaks anything, and Help reopens it.
- [ ] A first-time tester (someone who has not seen the template) finishes the tutorial in under 10 minutes without
      help. Record the time and where they hesitated.
- [ ] Litha can answer "what does this script do?" for every script from its header comment alone.

## F. Accessible and fair

- [ ] Colour is never the only signal for hazards, teams or rarity (shape, icon or text as well).
- [ ] Text at 1080p is at least 18 px; HUD scales with screen size (UDim2 scale, not only offsets).
- [ ] Keyboard and mouse, gamepad, and (from the mobile milestone) touch all reach every action the game needs.
- [ ] Camera shake, flashing and screen effects have a Game setting to reduce or turn them off, and no effect flashes
      more than 3 times per second.
- [ ] Horror and violence stay within a general audience: no gore, no realistic weapons branding, jump scares that
      can be turned down.

## G. Proven

- [ ] `tests/smoke.mscene` runs headless and prints `<SLUG>_SMOKE_OK` with no `error` lines, at default settings and
      at the knob extremes.
- [ ] A 10-minute soak in Play shows no growth in Instance count or script memory beyond the documented caps.
- [ ] The preview image and video show the real game at default settings, captured in Studio, not a mock-up.
- [ ] The template doc's acceptance checks are all ticked with links to evidence.
